ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, in $\triangle ABC$, $AB=AC$, and $\angle BAC=54^\circ$. The circle $\odot O$ with diameter $AB$ intersects $AC$ and $BC$ at points $D$ and $E$, respectively. A tangent to $\odot O$ passing through point $B$ intersects the extension of $AC$ at point $F$. Given $BE=CE$; find the measure of $\angle CBF$ in degrees.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $\angle BAC=54^\circ$ and $AB=AC$, it follows that $\angle ABC=63^\circ$.\\
Also, since $BF$ is the tangent to the circle $O$, it follows that $\angle ABF=90^\circ$.\\
Therefore, $\angle CBF=\angle ABF-\angle ABC=\boxed{27^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the triangle ABC in the figure, A is above, B is at the lower left, and C is on the right; the oblique line AC continues to extend downward to F. The circle passes through A and B, and the center O is on AB, indicating that AB is the diameter; the circle also intersects AC and BC at D and E respectively. The straight line BF is drawn from B and intersects the extension line of AC at F; it appears to be the tangent to the circle at point B, and the ray BC is located between BA and BF. Reasoning: It is known that AB=AC, and ∠BAC=54°, so triangle ABC is an isosceles triangle with vertex angle 54°, and the base angles are equal: ∠ABC=∠BCA=(180°-54°)/2=63°. Also because BF is the tangent to circle O through point B, and O is on the diameter AB, OB and AB are collinear, and the tangent BF is perpendicular to OB and also perpendicular to AB, therefore ∠ABF=90°. From the position in the figure, ∠CBF=∠ABF-∠ABC=90°-63°=27°.
